s0001: The Deposed Emperor of the Later reign had the taboo name Yu; his courtesy name was Derong and his childhood name Huizhen. He was Emperor Ming's eldest son.
The Deposed Emperor of the Later reign was named Yu, courtesy name Derong, childhood name Huizhen. He was the eldest son of Emperor Ming.

On renchen day in the sixth month an edict declared: "The canonical institutions of a founding king truly spring from the people's hidden needs; we now seek to spread instruction broadly and make it law in the four quarters.
s0018: I, lone and slight, from early age have received the precious succession; long have I spoken of civil affairs yet not yet heard and examined them myself; turning my thoughts again and again, I forget neither while awake nor in dreams to take them as my mirror.

I, young and alone, have from early youth received the precious succession; though I have long spoken of civil affairs, I have not yet heard and reviewed them myself; turning my thoughts again and again, I forget neither waking nor sleeping to take them as my mirror.
s0019: Let envoys be dispatched to travel separately through the four directions, observe and gather popular songs and rumors, and inquire into people's suffering.
Let envoys be dispatched to travel separately through the four directions, observe and gather popular songs and rumors, and inquire into the people's hardships.

If prefects and magistrates have authority and grace worthy of record, or show manifest probity and diligence, let reports on them be sent according to the facts.
